name: XAT
conductingBody: XLRI – Xavier School of Management, Jamshedpur (on behalf of XAMI)
frequency: Once a year (first Sunday of January)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (any discipline, minimum 3 years) or final-year students

notification.summary: XAT 2027 registration opened on 15 Jul 2026 on xatonline.in and is reported to remain open until about 6 Dec 2026; the computer-based exam is scheduled for Sunday 3 Jan 2027 (2–5 pm). Checked via web search on 2026-10-10 — dates are from coaching/news reports citing the official site and should be confirmed on xatonline.in.

pattern.stage: XAT (single computer-based test, Part I + Part II)
pattern.notes: Part I (Decision Making, VALR, QA-DI; 75 questions) and Part II (GK; 20 questions) — reported as 170 + 10 minutes within the 3-hour slot. Part I: +1 / −0.25, plus −0.10 for every unattempted question beyond 8. GK has no negative marking and is not counted in the XAT percentile (XLRI uses it at the final-selection stage). The essay section was discontinued from XAT 2024. Options in XAT are usually five; this mock uses four. Section-wise question counts vary slightly by year.

trendAnalysis.summary: XAT has kept a stable 3-hour format since dropping the essay in 2024, with about 75 Part I questions and 20 GK questions. QA-DI has been the toughest section in 2025 and 2026 (lengthy DI sets, algebra and geometry heavy), VALR is dominated by dense philosophical RC passages plus critical reasoning and the occasional poem, and Decision Making mixes ethical/managerial caselets with rule-based analytical sets. GK covers current affairs of the preceding year plus business and static GK and was easy in 2026. Overall difficulty: moderately difficult; time pressure and the penalty for leaving more than 8 questions make accuracy and coverage both important.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from memory-based papers and section-wise analyses of XAT 2024, XAT 2025 and XAT 2026 (held 7 Jan 2024, 5 Jan 2025 and 4 Jan 2026) by IMS, Career Launcher, TIME, Cracku, iQuanta and InsideIIM, located via web search; XLRI does not publish official papers and the full analyses could not be fetched, so recurring question types were consolidated from search snippets and the writer's own knowledge of the papers. Analyses agree on 21 DM, 26 VALR, 28 QA-DI and 20 GK questions, QA-DI as the toughest section (geometry-heavy, lengthy DI) and a poem-based item in VALR. Patterns are paraphrased; no actual question is reproduced. XAT uses five options; this mock keeps four.

archetypes.pattern: Employee discovers a safety/quality lapse that superiors want hidden; best option escalates through formal channels with evidence (not silence, not media leak, not quitting)
Conflict of interest, gifts or tainted funding; best option discloses, recuses or sets transparent conditions rather than outright rejection or quiet acceptance
Honesty vs loyalty/compassion: misreported numbers or rule-breaking by a sympathetic person; best option corrects the record while acting fairly
Strategy/operations caselet (market segments, capacity, demand peaks); choose the option that targets the actual constraint
Stakeholder trade-off under pressure from a large customer or cost cut; best option negotiates and protects compliance
Numerical decision caselet: compare alternatives by profit/contribution under given data and choose the best
Team conflict or a manager supervising former peers/friends; best first step is a private, fair conversation
Promotion, lay-off or performance decision balancing policy, fairness and individual circumstances
Rule-based eligibility set (scholarship, reimbursement, loan rules); apply all clauses to a case
Allocation of people to posts/tasks under constraints; a conditional 'if X then where is Y' question
Dense philosophical/socio-economic passage; author's main contention or central theme
Inference / author-would-agree / author's attitude on an abstract passage; options differ by degree
Role of an example or detail, or 'all of the following EXCEPT' detail check
Weaken/undermine or identify the assumption behind the passage's argument
Identify the flaw (reversed causation, correlation taken as cause) or the assumption in a short argument
Strengthen/weaken a business claim with an option that rules in or rules out alternative explanations
Deductive conclusion from conditional statements about people in an organisation
4–5 sentence para jumble with a historical or causal thread
Odd sentence out where one sentence shares the topic but not the paragraph's thread
Single/double blank vocabulary in a context sentence; logical consistency between the two blanks
Choose the grammatically correct sentence (inversion with 'Hardly/Scarcely', agreement, tense)
Short original-style poem; central idea or meaning of an image/line
Profit/discount on list price and percentage chains
Time-speed-distance: meetings, back-and-forth travel, relative speed
Work and pipes, including alternate-day work and a pipe closed midway
Mixtures and alligation (alloys, solutions)
Simple and compound interest (doubling, amounts in two years)
Algebraic identities: x + 1/x powers, a + b + c = 0 identities
Integer solutions: factor pairs, constrained non-negative solutions
Functions: functional equations, self-inverse functions, iterates
Progressions: AP/GP sums, infinite GP, Sₙ formula given
Triangle/polygon properties: angle bisector, circumradius, hexagon areas
Coordinate geometry: lines, distances, minimum areas
Mensuration of solids: cone/cylinder surface area and volume
Powers of primes in factorials, last digits and cyclicity
HCF/LCM pairs and divisibility conditions
Arrangements and distributions with restrictions (non-adjacent, at least k each)
Probability with dice, balls or selections
Table-based DI: shares, margins and comparisons where the largest absolute value is the trap
Caselet DI with what-if changes or overlapping categories
Appointments and heads of governments/institutions in the past year
Awards and prizes of the past year (Nobel, Booker, Peace)
International summits, chairships and sporting-event hosts
Economy and policy institutions: commissions, payment systems, budget announcements
Corporate news: mergers, joint ventures, brand ownership
Static geography of India
History and polity basics (battles, texts, constitutional provisions)
Science and sports facts linked to recent events

resources.notes: XLRI publishes a free official mock test for registered candidates on xatonline.in shortly before the exam. Official answer keys/question papers are not routinely published; previous papers in circulation are memory-based reconstructions by coaching institutes.

questions.question: Two cyclists start at the same time from towns P and Q, 90 km apart, riding towards each other at 20 km/h and 25 km/h respectively. Each, on reaching the other town, turns back immediately at the same speed. How far from P do they meet for the second time?
questions.explanation: By the second meeting they have together covered 3 × 90 = 270 km, taking 270/45 = 6 hours. The cyclist from P has ridden 120 km: 90 km to Q and 30 km back, i.e. 60 km from P.

relevance.note: Second meeting after turnaround at 60 km from P (3D total distance); good XAT TSD with 30/45 traps

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of integers (x, y) satisfy x² − y² = 45?
questions.explanation: (x − y)(x + y) = 45. Both factors must have the same parity; since 45 is odd, all its factor pairs are odd. Ordered factor pairs (a, b) with ab = 45: (1, 45), (3, 15), (5, 9), (9, 5), (15, 3), (45, 1) and their negatives — 12 pairs, each giving integer x = (a + b)/2, y = (b − a)/2. So 12.

relevance.note: x^2-y^2=45 has 12 integer pairs incl. negatives, with 6 as the positive-only trap; strong XAT integer-solution item

questions.question: A function f satisfies f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 3x for every non-zero real x. What is f(2)?

relevance.note: f(x)+2f(1/x)=3x -> f(2)=-1; typical XAT functional equation

questions.question: The sum of an infinite geometric progression is 20, and the sum of the squares of its terms is 100. What is the first term?

relevance.note: Infinite GP sum 20 and squares 100 -> a=8; neat XAT-level progression

questions.question: A straight line passes through the point (2, 3) and cuts the positive x-axis and the positive y-axis. What is the minimum possible area of the triangle it forms with the coordinate axes?
questions.explanation: Line x/a + y/b = 1 with 2/a + 3/b = 1. By AM–GM, 1 = 2/a + 3/b ≥ 2√(6/(ab)), so ab ≥ 24 and the area ab/2 ≥ 12, with equality when 2/a = 3/b = 1/2, i.e. a = 4, b = 6.

relevance.note: Min intercept-triangle area through (2,3) = 12; classic XAT coordinate optimisation

questions.question: A bakery sells 1,000 cakes a week at ₹400 each. The variable cost is ₹250 per cake and fixed costs are ₹90,000 a week. The owner is considering two options: (i) cut the price by 10%, which a survey suggests will raise weekly sales by 20%; or (ii) run an advertising campaign costing ₹20,000 a week, expected to raise sales by 15% at the current price. Which decision maximises weekly profit?
options: Cut the price, since it gives the larger increase in sales.
Make no change, since both options reduce profit.
questions.explanation: Current profit = 1,000 × 150 − 90,000 = ₹60,000. Price cut: 1,200 × (360 − 250) − 90,000 = ₹42,000. Advertising: 1,150 × 150 − 90,000 − 20,000 = ₹62,500. Advertising is the only option that raises profit.

relevance.note: Price cut gives 42,000 vs ads 62,500 vs current 60,000; XAT numerical DM with sales-volume trap

questions.question: A factory makes two products. Product X earns a profit of ₹40 per unit and needs 2 machine-hours; product Y earns ₹50 per unit and needs 4 machine-hours. 400 machine-hours are available each week, and at most 150 units of X and 100 units of Y can be sold per week. Which weekly production plan maximises profit?
options: 50 units of X and 75 units of Y
150 units of X and 25 units of Y
100 units of X and 50 units of Y
questions.explanation: X earns ₹20 per machine-hour and Y ₹12.5, so make the maximum 150 X (300 hours) and use the remaining 100 hours for 25 Y: profit 6,000 + 1,250 = ₹7,250. The other plans give ₹6,500, ₹5,750 and ₹6,000.

relevance.note: Machine-hour constrained mix: X 150 + Y 25 = 7,250 beats others; contribution-per-hour XAT DM

questions.question: A company's travel policy says: (1) Employees at grade M3 and above may fly business class on flights longer than 4 hours; all others fly economy. (2) Any employee may upgrade at his or her own cost. (3) International travel requires prior approval of the department head; if the employee is travelling with a client, approval of the CFO is also required. Rohit, at grade M2, will fly to Singapore (a 5.5-hour flight) with a client and wants the company to pay for business class. What is the correct position?
options: The company will pay for business class, with approval from the CFO only.
The company will pay only for economy class, with approval from his department head only.
The company will pay for business class, with approval from his department head.
The company will pay only for economy class, and Rohit needs approval from both his department head and the CFO.
questions.explanation: Rule 1: as an M2, Rohit is entitled to economy regardless of flight length (he may upgrade at his own cost under rule 2). Rule 3: international travel with a client needs both the department head's and the CFO's approval.

relevance.note: M2 economy only; client trip needs dept head and CFO; faithful XAT rule-application

questions.question: How many ordered triples of positive odd integers (x, y, z) satisfy x + y + z = 15?
questions.explanation: Write x = 2a + 1, y = 2b + 1, z = 2c + 1 with a, b, c ≥ 0. Then 2(a + b + c) = 12, so a + b + c = 6, which has C(8, 2) = 28 non-negative solutions.

relevance.note: Odd positive triples summing to 15 -> 28 via substitution; good XAT counting
